overview: This Senate resolution names July 26, 2025, as the "National Day of the American Cowboy." It praises cowboys and cowgirls for helping settle the American West, for the values the cowboy is often seen to represent, such as hard work, honesty and patriotism, and for caring for the land. It also notes the role of ranchers in the economy and the popularity of rodeo. The resolution encourages people across the country to mark the day with ceremonies and activities. It is symbolic and does not create a federal holiday or change any law. The Senate agreed to it in July 2025.
for: Supporters say it honors a lasting part of American history and the ranchers and rodeo participants who still carry on those traditions today.
against: Critics say it is purely symbolic and does not change any law, funding or support for ranchers or rural communities.
